lane.label: Renting an exact-match city domain, by phone
lane.sells: One business per city and trade rents the exact domain people type — renton-towing.com — for $99/month.
lane.goal: They give you a number and an email, and agree to receive a checkout link today.

grounding_label: what the rep can actually prove about this domain and its price

archetypes.label: Towing operator, no website
traits: gets ten spam calls a day
archetypes.opening_state: Expects a robocall. Will hang up on anything that sounds read.

archetypes.label: Burned by an SEO agency
traits: paid a monthly retainer for a year
never saw a report he understood
archetypes.opening_state: Waiting for you to say the thing the last guy said, so he can hang up.

archetypes.label: Already has a website
traits: someone in the family built it
archetypes.opening_state: Hears "website" and starts composing a polite no.

archetypes.label: Not the owner
archetypes.opening_state: Deciding in four seconds whether to pass you along.

objections.good_move: Good — this is not a replacement. It is a second front door on the name people type, and it can point at the site they already have.
objections.trap: Arguing their site is bad. They built it, or someone in their family did.

objections.says: Does it come up on Google?
objections.good_move: Not yet, it's new, and say so plainly — then the real close: $99 now, $399 once one reaches page one, and their rate is locked either way.
objections.trap: Any version of "it will rank." You do not know that, and it is the promise that ends up in a complaint.

objections.good_move: The name, exclusively, in their town — and let them do the one-job-pays-for-it math out loud themselves.
objections.trap: Doing that math for them, in calls per week. That is a result promise wearing arithmetic.

objections.says: I paid an SEO guy for a year and got nothing.
objections.good_move: Agree — that is why this is rent on a specific name they can look at, not a retainer for work they cannot see. Month to month, cancel whenever.
objections.trap: Defending the industry, or implying the last guy was a crook. He might have been their brother-in-law.

objections.says: What stops you renting it to the guy across town?
objections.good_move: Nothing does, until they take it — one per city and trade is the product, and that is exactly why it is worth having.
objections.trap: Turning a true fact into a fake deadline. First-come is real; "I have someone else on the line" is not.

objections.good_move: No. Month to month, cancel whenever — and their rate stays theirs for as long as they keep it.
objections.trap: Overselling the lock-in as a favour. It is simply true; say it and move on.

objections.good_move: Take it, name a time, write it down. Then actually call.
objections.trap: Inventing a deadline to stop them going. Never do this.

objections.good_move: A small studio that builds these — send them quicksites.ai and let them look while you are on the line.
objections.trap: Inflating the company. The site is small and honest; being caught padding it costs the call.

objections.good_move: Fine — get the address, send it while still on the phone, and ask them to open it now so the domain is on their screen before you hang up.
objections.trap: Accepting the email as a win. An unopened email is a no with a delay.

objections.good_move: Ask when the owner is around and whether it is worth a call back then — briefly, without pitching the gatekeeper.
objections.trap: Pitching anyway. They cannot buy, and a bad summary is what reaches the owner instead of you.

honesty_rules.rule: Never promise a ranking, a call volume, or a result.
honesty_rules.why: Nobody knows. A promise like that ends up in a complaint with the rep’s name on it, and it is the single rule the whole brief is strict about.
violating_examples: this'll get you on page one
you'll get five calls a week
you will rank for towing in Renton
it pays for itself in the first month

honesty_rules.rule: Never invent a deadline, a competing buyer, or a price that is about to expire.
honesty_rules.why: First-come is true; a countdown is not. A fake deadline is the fastest way to turn a real advantage into a lie.
violating_examples: I have another towing company looking at this one right now
if you do not take it today I have to release it

honesty_rules.rule: Never add claims about their business that they have not made — licensing, insurance, response times, reviews.
honesty_rules.why: We spent a day stripping exactly those invented lines off these sites. Saying them out loud puts them back where nothing can catch them.
violating_examples: we'll put licensed and insured on there for you
it says you respond within the hour
I'll add some reviews to fill it out
